penalties_summary: None specified in this Discussion Paper. The paper explicitly disclaims imposing binding monitoring expectations or immediate mandates, prioritizing voluntary industry efforts, agile governance, safe harbors, and ongoing supervisory dialogue—while reiterating that existing technology-neutral financial statutes (such as the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act and APPI) and supervisory guidelines remain enforceable regardless of AI use.
implementation_notes: Version 1.1 (March 2026) of the Financial Services Agency's AI Discussion Paper, updating Ver. 1.0 with insights from the June–December 2025 FSA AI Public-Private Forum and reflecting Japan's May 2025 AI Promotion Act and December 2025 Basic AI Plan. Covers conventional AI, generative AI (internal, indirect customer, and direct customer deployments), and emerging AI agents / agentic AI across 130 surveyed financial institutions, detailing emerging customer-facing guardrails (Box 4), AI-agent lifecycle/permission platforms, APPI and FIEA regulatory clarifications, systemic financial-stability risks, regional-bank GenAI DX pilots (Box 5), and FSA's own SupTech AI initiatives.
